title: The Invisible $35,000 Raise: Seeing the Consumer-Surplus Miracles Already Here—and Unfreezing What Still Hurts
tagline: Honoring real rent and medical pain while revealing $35,000/yr of invisible digital, energy, and biomedical abundance already in every pocket—and pulling housing, healthcare, and childcare onto that exact same curve.
cynicBelief: Modern progress is a mirage—everything that actually matters to a working family gets more expensive every decade, technology only produces addictive toys for billionaires, and ordinary households haven't gained real ground since 1995.
breakthroughCounter: We live inside a stark Two-Speed Economy: every sector open to clean-tech learning curves, software, and automation plunged 70%–99.8% in price (solar PV -99.8%, batteries -97%, genome sequencing $100M to $100, global video calls $180/hr to $0, encyclopedias and AI tutors $0). Erik Brynjolfsson's PNAS GDP-B choice experiments prove households already enjoy $25,000–$35,000+/yr in uncounted welfare, and Ronnie Chatterji's NBER WP 34255 shows >70% of AI use serves unpriced family life—pointing directly to how we unfreeze housing, medical billing, and care next.
socialNormShift: Replacing 1930s price-only GDP blindfolds with Stanford GDP-B consumer-surplus accounting while systematically removing the 20th-century zoning, medical-coding, and utility monopolies that kept rent, healthcare, and childcare off the abundance learning curve.

humanStory.protagonist: Marisol Vega (41, Home-Health Aide & Mother of Two) & Abuela Lucía (69)
humanStory.location: Jackson Heights, Queens, New York & Puebla, Mexico
humanStory.snippet: In 1998, Marisol's mom spent $120/month on scratchy 12-minute calling cards; in 2026, Marisol already holds $35,000/yr of invisible miracles ($0 nightly HD bedtime stories with Abuela, an AI reading tutor for her dyslexic son, $4 generic heart meds)—and by 2033, mass-timber YIMBY housing and $65 Direct Primary Care finally pull her rent and doctor bills onto that same deflationary curve.

quote.text: GDP measures what we pay for, not what actually improves our lives. When an encyclopedia, a global video call, or a life-guiding tool drops in price from thousands of dollars to zero, GDP records nothing—even as ordinary families gain tens of thousands of dollars in real well-being.
quote.author: Prof. Erik Brynjolfsson
quote.role: Jerry Yang and Akiko Yamazaki Professor & Director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab (PNAS GDP-B Co-Author)

title: Healing the Zero-Sum Brain: Why Free Energy & Automation Are the Keys to Ending Human Scarcity Politics
tagline: Uniting Mullainathan & Shafir's 13-IQ-point cognitive bandwidth science and Benjamin Friedman's 200-year moral history with near-free clean energy, robotics, and citizen dividends to cure zero-sum fear.
cynicBelief: Human beings are hardwired by evolution to be tribal, envious, and zero-sum—no matter how much clean energy or automation we invent, politics will stay nasty, fearful, and polarized forever.
breakthroughCounter: Behavioral science and history prove the opposite: Sendhil Mullainathan and Eldar Shafir (Science, 2013) demonstrated that financial scarcity literally taxes 13–14 IQ points of human cognitive bandwidth (worse than losing a full night's sleep), while Benjamin M. Friedman showed across two centuries that broadly shared material abundance reliably makes societies more generous, tolerant, and open. Pairing near-free clean energy and automation with citizen dividends and 90% wage bridges heals survival tunneling at its physical root.
socialNormShift: Recognizing technical abundance (sub-penny clean energy + physical/knowledge automation) and humane social conventions (universal citizen dividends, 90% transition bridges, demonetized essentials) as two halves of a single key that restores human cognitive bandwidth and civic trust.

humanStory.protagonist: Derrick Hollis (44, Former Stamping Machinist & Robotics Guild Mentor) & Ananya Nair (36, Solar-Ag Steward)
humanStory.location: Youngstown, Ohio & Villupuram District, Tamil Nadu, India
humanStory.snippet: In 2024, plant-closure anxiety kept Derrick locked in survival-tunneling distrust of machines and newcomers; by 2033, backed by a 90% Danish-style Guild Wage Bridge, $14/mo clean power, and Ohio's Citizen Compute Dividend, Derrick coaches teen robotics teams and co-chairs a cross-partisan town assembly welcoming new neighbors.

quote.text: Scarcity doesn't just mean having less money in your wallet—it captures the mind itself, taxing thirteen IQ points of mental bandwidth. Relieve chronic material scarcity, and you don't make people lazy; you give human beings their full intelligence, patience, and generosity back.
quote.author: Prof. Sendhil Mullainathan
quote.role: Professor of Computation and Behavioral Science, MIT (Co-Author of Scarcity & 2013 Science Bandwidth Study)
